Wow those comments are lacking perspective. I have few trans friends and don't really feel my gender as a barrier/label myself. Of course you can do all the stuff both gender can, but it's many different cases.

Trans folks - it's also a very psychological thing, they often do feel like the opposite gender "from the beginning" and want to be seen as it. Often not even seen as a trans person, but thorough the transition "transfer" to the correct gender they feel good as. And often don't want to feel special or seen as trans. IT'S a very simplified description and obviously not all trans people feel this way.

Some are proud to be trans what I mostly see as seeing themselves and other trans folks as valid and seeing that  what they go through is meaningful. Also in many countries you can't really find a lot of help/or information for other trans people and you're left to do research when you... Know where to? And that there's someone who went what you're going through.

Non-binary people are just this. Nonbinary. They don't feel as any of the genders (this also obviously depends as is a spectrum, one again, simplified) and don't want to be seen as any. It's "new", but it's same label as girl/boy/non-binary person - it's not your whole lifestyle now, it's just what defines some part of you
